DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Three Strings, One Night

STS-HS10-L4-1400P-HSELA910-PCI-NAV-01 • HS English 9–10 • Narrative Techniques and Multiple Plot Lines
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Booth Tapes is recorded in diners because a diner is where three different conversations happen at three different tables on the same night, and none of the people know they are in the same story. Rosalie's draft is built that way on purpose: one plot line leaves, one waits, one works the last shift, and all three arrive at the same booth by midnight. The teacher is clipping up the third line before anybody has decided whether it earns its place.
If Rosalie cut the third plot line, what would the other two lines have to do differently for the ending to still land?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Maya doing?
Look at the picture. Make a claim about what Maya is doing and what she wants the group to think about, ground it in specific visual evidence, and extend it to how her point shapes the story the group is telling. Speak in academic register.
2
What is Desmond holding?
Look at the picture. Make a claim about what Desmond is holding and what his role is in this recording, ground it in specific visual evidence, and extend it to why an interview needs one person holding it and another answering. Speak in academic register.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Make a claim about what the teacher is doing and how it changes the wall, ground it in specific visual evidence, and extend it to what her action suggests about how the group builds a story. Speak in academic register.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Make a claim about what kind of place this is and how you know, ground it in specific visual evidence, and extend it to why this setting suits the recording happening in it. Speak in academic register.
5
Tell me about the cards on the wall.
Look at the picture. Make a claim about how the cards are arranged and what the arrangement is meant to show, ground it in specific visual evidence, and extend it to what the arrangement says about the story the group is building. Speak in academic register.
6
What is Rosalie wearing?
Look at the picture. Make a claim about what Rosalie is wearing and how her clothing sets her apart, ground it in specific visual evidence, and extend it to why clear differences matter when a listener cannot see the room. Speak in academic register.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.W.9-10.3.b — Narrative techniques: dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
